subject: SDK + Dedicated Runtime: inconsistent cache hits and streaming timeouts
messages:
From: Elena Miranda <elena.miranda@brighthealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@brighthealth.com
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: initial integration: streaming times out when cache enabled

Hi Jonas —

We're seeing an intermittent issue when our engineers toggle the SDK's 'enable_prefix_cache' flag against your Dedicated endpoint. For some requests we get fast token responses (streaming chunks arrive within 40-60ms), but for other identical inputs the client times out after 8s with partial chunks; the server logs show a cache-miss then a KV cache rebuild but the rebuild logs stop early. Attached a small repro run and the raw runtime logs (brighthealth_logs.zip).

Repro steps (summary):
- SDK v0.17.2 (Python)
- call .stream_generate(prompt, stream=True) with enable_prefix_cache=True
- repeat same prompt 10x at 1s intervals
- 2-3 out of 10 calls return within 100ms, 1-2 out of 10 time out after 8s (client-side)

Can you confirm whether Dedicated runtimes should behave identically to hosted regarding prefix cache TTL and streaming? Our CS/Infra team needs to know if this is expected variance before we push to prod.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Miranda
Platform Engineer, BrightHealth

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: initial integration: streaming times out when cache enabled

Forwarding BrightHealth's repro. This looks like a field report that touches the runtime cache behavior and streaming timeouts. Quick asks:
- Dev: can you confirm whether Dedicated runtimes have any different cache invalidation or async KV rebuild behavior compared to hosted?
- PM (Laura): is there a current plan to make cache behavior deterministic across deployment types in the v0.18 rollout?
- SE (Marissa): any recommended mitigations we should suggest to the customer immediately (SDK config or routing workaround)?

Customer is sensitive (large upcoming pilot), so we should prioritize a short-latency investigation and a mitigation if possible. Logs attached.

Jonas Weber
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: initial integration: streaming times out when cache enabled

Thanks for the ping and the repro, attaching my quick read. High-level notes:
- Dedicated and Hosted use the same serving runtime code, but Dedicated can be configured with different cache size and eager-rebuild settings per-tenant. I will check the tenant config used in BrightHealth's Dedicated cluster.
- The symptom (cache-miss then rebuild that "stops early") suggests the KV rebuild goroutine might be hitting an OOM backpressure path or being preempted by a GC pause on older Go images we still run in a subset of Dedicated nodes.
- Streaming timeouts at ~8s sounds like our client-side default (sdk streaming read timeout) combined with slow server-side first-chunk emission when cache rebuild is triggered.

Immediate action items I'm starting:
1) Pull the Dedicated tenant config for BH and compare cache settings to Hosted defaults.
2) Re-run the repro in an internal mirror with SDK v0.17.2 and our Dedicated image; reproduce the 1-in-4 timeout probability.
3) If we reproduce, try forcing eager KV rebuild on hit to see if that reduces variance.

Question for SE/PM: can we ask the customer to temporarily set sdk.stream_timeout=20s and enable sdk.disable_prefix_cache=true on their staging fleet so they can continue the pilot while we dig in? That would avoid blocking their rollout.

I'll post logs and experiment results by tomorrow morning.

— Dev

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: elena.miranda@brighthealth.com, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: initial integration: streaming times out when cache enabled

Hi Elena —
Appreciate the detailed repro and logs. Two quick mitigation suggestions you can apply now that don't require infra changes:

1) Set stream_timeout to 20s (as Dev suggested) in your SDK consumer config. This prevents client-side aborts while we stabilize.
2) If your flow tolerates slightly higher cost for determinism, set enable_prefix_cache=false in staging so every request hits CPU path but avoids KV rebuild nondeterminism.

We'll keep you informed about whether we need a runtime patch. If you can grant us access to the brighthealth dedicated tenant id (or paste the tenant id from the admin page), that will let Dev check the tenant-level cache policy right away.

I can join a quick 30-min call today to walk the customer through toggling those flags. Jonas — can you coordinate meeting times?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
